findings.title: [narrative] draft->critique->revise is live only for the capture flow; photo builds never call it and ship an ungated LLM overview from the [steps] model

findings.title: Claim-coverage gate silently drops every claim when narrative generation fails, and the narrative stage's [verify] ids never reach the sidecar report

Grep test_server.py for a raising narrative stub -> none (only :1002 success case). Peer A-05 confirms. See F-16 for the polish-enabled crash on the same path.
findings.proposed_fix: In `_generate`: on exception set `narrative_text, _covered, _verify_ids = ensure_claim_coverage("", claims)` so every claim is emitted as a [verify] blockquote; keep `_verify_ids` and extend `verify_claim_ids`/`claims_by_id` with them before `build_sidecar_report`. Add a test with a raising narrative stub asserting `md.count('[verify]') == len(claims)` and `report['verify_claims']` lists them.

findings.title: Photo build with the committed default [vision].enabled=true replaces the uploaded transcript with captions; transcript text is never placed verbatim under steps

findings.title: Capture flow re-dumps paraphrased transcript lines at the top of the document as [verify] blockquotes even though the same lines are already placed under steps

Coverage is exact substring: claim_coverage.py:23 `return stripped.lower() in text.lower()`; :69-71 appends every uncovered claim verbatim. findings.proposed_fix: Treat step-level placements as coverage: run `ensure_claim_coverage` against `narrative_text + "\n" + "\n".join(r.get("narration","") for r in step_results)` (or build claims only from `synthetic_narration` when a transcript was placed), so only genuinely unplaced claims become [verify] blockquotes.

findings.title: Capture agent declares no DPI awareness; click, screenshot and UIA-rect coordinate frames depend on whichever third-party library initializes first
findings.evidence: Grep `DPI|dpi|SetProcess|SetThread|shcore` over src/, tests/, scripts/ *.py -> no matches; sopforge.spec:29 `runtime_hooks=[]`. recorder.py:141-143 `element, window = resolve_at(x, y)` / `self._shots.capture(x, y)` / `screen_x, screen_y = x - origin_x, y - origin_y` -- pixel offsets only, no scale factor; pywinauto is imported lazily at uia.py:71 `from pywinauto import Desktop` on the first click, after the pynput hook is already installed. Whether pywinauto changes the process DPI context on import could not be checked (shell denied; site-packages not found under the repo/user paths searched), so the 'frame depends on import order' part remains an unverified risk, as peer A-09 notes. tests/test_recorder.py:152-156 cover 100%-scale, non-negative origins only.
findings.proposed_fix: At the top of `capture/__main__.py` call `ctypes.windll.user32.SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(-4)` (PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) with `shcore.SetProcessDpiAwareness(2)` fallback so hooks, mss and pywinauto share one physical-pixel frame; record `screen.scale` in the manifest; add negative-origin and mixed-DPI cases to test_recorder.py.

findings.title: A click outside every monitor rect is attributed to monitor 1 and translated by monitor 1's origin; only reachable if hook and mss coordinate frames disagree
findings.evidence: shots.py:30-36 `for idx, mon in enumerate(sct.monitors[1:], start=1): if (mon["left"] <= x < ... ): return idx` / `return 1`; :56-57 `monitor = sct.monitors[monitor_idx]; origin = (monitor["left"], monitor["top"])`; recorder.py:143 subtracts that origin. Peer's dispute (A-09 response to F-12) is partly right: Windows confines the cursor to the monitor union, so with pynput and mss in the same DPI context this branch should be unreachable; it is reached only under the F-11 frame-mismatch precondition, which I could not demonstrate. Retained as low because the fallback is silent (no log, no manifest flag) when it does fire.
findings.proposed_fix: Log a warning and set a manifest flag when `monitor_for_point` falls through to 1 (so a frame mismatch becomes visible rather than silently mis-placing the marker); fix the frame itself per F-11 rather than clamping.
